title: Speckle bridges low-level 3D data so Powerhouse document models can stay high-level
content:
The integration strategy for construction pairs two layers (BAI weekly, 00:15:57–00:22:09):

- **Speckle** (open-source) manages low-level, industry-specific 3D data — synchronizing models across Revit, Blender, AutoCAD, with a robust, mature ecosystem. It handles details like door counts or piping data.
- **Powerhouse document models** sit at the high level — project management, requirements, approvals — referencing the low-level data.

The payoff: documents automatically update when the underlying 3D models change, delivering value **without requiring clients to replace their existing software stacks** (00:17:17).

Diligence notes (BIM briefing):
- Speckle's server is partially enterprise-licensed — the Apache vs enterprise boundary needs mapping (speckle-server repo; specklepy's IFC handling includes per-file licenses)
- Under the hood Speckle partially uses **ifcopenshell** for IFC work, so the open toolchain remains reachable if Speckle's licensing becomes a constraint

This is the general shape of the positioning: don't compete with mature low-level tools — compose with them and own the document/process layer above.
description: Integration strategy: Speckle syncs 3D data across Revit/Blender/AutoCAD; Powerhouse document models sit above it, auto-updating when models change — no stack replacement required.
